The VAS dismissed the Migration Directorate’s cassation appeal and upheld the annulment of its refusal and remittal for a new decision. It held that, for derivative residence only, a same-sex spouse lawfully married in another Member State qualifies under the then-applicable national family-member definition read with Directive 2004/38 and Coman. The Court stated that this does not recognize the marriage generally for Bulgarian civil-status law. It also said the lower court’s Article 21 TFEU citation was erroneous but did not affect the result.

It addresses a specific derivative-residence claim by a same-sex spouse of a mobile EU citizen and does not decide general marriage registration, durable partnership, or rights of family members of non-mobile Bulgarian citizens.

The judgment did not resolve every evidentiary issue: the VAS noted that the authority had based its refusal on the marriage-recognition ground and remitted the matter for fresh administrative consideration.
Accepted as an external-only official court record; no local copy is retained. The targeted web search is not a complete or repeatable VAS/lower-court discovery batch.

bg-vas-case-3002-2026.reviewed_content: The complete official decision text and native PDF were reviewed. The VAS dismissed the Migration Directorate’s cassation appeal and left in force the Sofia City Administrative Court decision annulling the entry ban. It applied the individualized-threat standard in Article 27 of Directive 2004/38, requiring concrete evidence of a genuine, present and sufficiently serious threat. On the record before it, the Court found no established evidence that the person helped transport irregular migrants; calling 112 about people in distress and NGO membership/volunteering did not establish the asserted threat.
limitations: The judgment is fact-specific and does not decide every application of Articles 26–27, establish a general authority practice, or replace current statutory text.
It is a fixed decision dated 17 March 2026; later case law and amendments were not reviewed as part of this individual record.
The VAS exact-acronym search returned 23 cases, but only this decision was fully screened in the 25 October batch. The other matches and separate lower-court case-law surfaces remain unresolved.
